title: What an absolute gift to have this much talent on one stage. ❤️ The W...
transcript: I went to see the Whoopi Goldberg monologues because it has one of the most ridiculously stacked casts in New York City right now. What I was unprepared for is how much these monologues end up affecting me. Whoopi Goldberg wrote and performed the Whoopi Goldberg monologues in 1984 as a one person show. Now it has been reimagined with five different black actresses each doing their own monologue. And somehow, even though these monologues have been written more than 40 years ago, they feel shockingly relevant. These are stories of womanhood and blackness, identity, aging, beauty standards, and wanting to be seen for who you are. And it feels like they could have been written today. The cast is unbelievable with Carrie Washington, Dominic Fishback, Danielle Pinckney, Keisha Lewis, and Kara Young. They are hilarious, vulnerable, captivating storytellers. I couldn't look away. I didn't wanna miss a second. And director Whitney White continues to prove that she's one of the best working right now. The transitions and the staging are mesmerizing. Even though these are monologues, it really feels like these women are having a shared conversation between generations. It's both a Celebration of all the things that we have in common and a reminder of how little things have actually changed. You have until August 30th to see the Whoopi monologues at Lincoln Center Theater.
reasoning: Enthusiastic first-hand review praising the cast, direction, and emotional impact with a clear call to see it before closing.
